newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 18.

text.p: Kopu loss may cost Alliance funding, staff: The Alliance could lose about $60,000 of funding for its parliamentary office and could have to make staff redundant because of dissident MP Alamein Kopu's defection. Page 1.
Jobless rise with softer economy: Unemployment rose in the past few months because economic growth was softer than predicted, Employment Minister Peter McCardle said on Thursday. Page 2.

Wellington best in retail trade: The May retail trade figures confirm that retailing around New Zealand is sluggish, though Wellington trading in restaurants, cafes, recreational goods and chemists is giving the region an edge on the rest. Page 13.

Comfort zone widening, says Bankers Trust: The Reserve Bank was becoming more confortable with easier monetary conditions but would not officially ease them, Bankers Trust said on Thursday in the wake of weak retail sales data. Page 13.

Deane satisfied with Telecom performance: Telecom New Zealand's performance in the first quarter of the 1997-98 year was satisfactory in a flat economy, chief executive Roderick Deane said after the annual meeting in Wellington on Thursday. Page 13.

Companies continue action in court: Clear Communications' latest court move against Telecom and the government was "another attempt to justify its refusal to pay its bills", Telecom spokesman Clive Litt said on Thursday. Page 13.
Macraes scraps gold project: A $120 million expansion programme for Macraes Mining's operations near Dunedin has become a casualty of sliding gold prices.
Lion Nathan steals march in huge Chinese market: Lion Nathan may have stolen a march on other international brewers eyeing the huge beer market in mainland China.
Stirling Sports out to buy and go public: Sporting goods chain Stirling Sports is looking to expand by buying up other retail businesses.

Winebox commissioner moves to block inquiry report release: The winebox inquiry commissioner, former Chief Justice Sir Ronald Davison, has been in breach of a High Court order for the past week for not producing documentation on the case in which he is accused of bias.

Resign call by Lange: Former Alliance MP Alamein Kopu should resign from Parliament immediately because she did not represent "her people", former prime minister David Lange said on Thursday night. Page 3.

Govt warning fails to deter private crimebusters: A private company that plans to investigate and prosecute criminal cases is not deterred by the Solicitor-General warning Crown solicitors not to work for it. Page 5.

Myers ranked richest in NZ: Douglas Myers, chief executive of Lion Nathan and a major shareholder in the company, is New Zealand's richest person with assets totalling $325 million, according to the "National Business Review" rich list. Page 23.
